goal: Speeds up ChaCha20 encryption 2-4x using SIMD, reducing CPU used by BIP324 encrypted P2P transport.
Benefits node operators and anyone running the network thread, since profiling shows ChaCha20 eating a large share of net-thread CPU.
reviewability: Paused, waiting on author: l0rinc's detailed changes-requested review (restructuring, tests, benchmarks) has gone unanswered for over two weeks.
The PR itself is explicitly a draft still being reworked, with the author previously rewriting the whole approach twice.
agreement: One concept ACK with no stated objection (jonatack).

l0rinc has repeatedly requested changes: correctness/test coverage gaps, platform-specific performance regressions, and a request to split into reviewable commits, not yet addressed in the latest round (l0rinc).
Author (theuni) has engaged substantively throughout, rewriting the implementation multiple times in response to feedback, but has not replied to the most recent round of review.

categories.name: utils
why: P2 because it delivers a measured 2-4x speedup to a cryptographic primitive (ChaCha20) used pervasively in P2P transport and profiled at roughly 30% of net-thread CPU time.
It also surfaced and fixed a real correctness bug (a big-endian XOR-order error), showing the change touches correctness as well as speed.
Not P1 because it is a performance optimization of already-correct behavior rather than a fix for a live bug, and per-platform tuning is still unstable (regressions found on RPi5/GCC and Umbrel IBD).

result.summary: This draft PR adds a SIMD-vectorized ChaCha20 implementation intended to give a 2-4x speedup over the scalar implementation, targeting x86-64 and ARM64 via compiler vector builtins rather than hand-written intrinsics or assembly. The author has gone through multiple design iterations (256-bit vectors, then a pluggable vector abstraction, then a simplified 128-bit-only design) driven by extensive review feedback about correctness (a big-endian bug), portability, and GCC/Clang codegen quality differences. It remains a draft with acknowledged rough edges: messy commit history, missing documentation, and untested dispatch tuning for various platforms.
result.problem: ChaCha20 is used heavily in the BIP324 encrypted P2P transport, and profiling by the author showed it consuming roughly 30% of the network thread's CPU time; a faster implementation reduces CPU load for every node using encrypted transport, and l0rinc's IBD benchmarks showed a measurable (if modest, ~3%) speedup on real workloads.

open_concerns: l0rinc's 2026-08-30 CHANGES_REQUESTED review: lack of test coverage for the new dispatch/group logic, per-target tuning choices (block-group cutoffs) that may not be optimal or well-tested, a request to split the PR into smaller reviewable commits (backend, adoption, benchmarks, tests), reuse of existing ALWAYS_INLINE/endian helpers, and a reported IBD slowdown on Umbrel with this PR vs master that needs re-measurement.

Whether the horizontal vs vertical state layout and per-target block-count dispatch tables are the right long-term design, since tuning is expected to need periodic revisiting as compilers/architectures change.
Correctness confidence: current fuzzing does not exercise every dispatch group size; l0rinc proposed fuzz/test/benchmark extensions to cover this.
resolved_concerns: Big-endian correctness bug (XOR/byteswap ordering) found by l0rinc, fixed by theuni.
GCC codegen bug causing a severe slowdown, root-caused by theuni to a GCC vectorizer limitation and worked around via a 128-bit implementation.

Early nits about recursive-template style vs if-constexpr/index_sequence approaches were discussed at length; author explained why lambdas/index_sequence tricks caused inlining regressions in practice, and reviewers accepted the recursive-template approach as a reasonable tradeoff.
discussion.author_status: active but silent since 2025-08-25; posted a major rewrite 2026-08-21, but has not yet responded to l0rinc's detailed 2026-08-29/30 review round.

categories.name: utils
categories.evidence: The PR modifies src/crypto/chacha20*.{cpp,h,ipp} — a cryptographic primitive under the utils category's 'randomness and cryptographic primitives' scope, with no consumer-specific behavior change beyond speed and correctness.
categories.rationale: P2 because the change delivers a substantial, benchmark-confirmed performance improvement (2-4x on the microbenchmark, ~3% end-to-end IBD speedup measured by l0rinc) to a primitive the author profiled at ~30% of net-thread CPU time in BIP324 handling. It also surfaced and fixed a real correctness bug (big-endian XOR ordering), giving it a minor security/stability dimension. It is not P1 because it optimizes already-correct scalar behavior rather than fixing a live defect or unblocking other critical work, and the implementation is still unstable across platforms (regressions on RPi5/GCC and an Umbrel IBD slowdown reported by l0rinc), meaning the benefit is not yet reliably realized everywhere.

uncertainties: Whether the reported Umbrel IBD slowdown (l0rinc, 2026-08-30) is a real regression or a benchmarking artifact; this materially affects how much performance benefit can be claimed.

Whether the project intends this as the final design or expects it to be superseded by l0rinc's alternative branch (#286), which could change how much review investment in the current code is worthwhile.

No explicit project.toml-level confirmation of how draft status interacts with the Paused determination beyond the general rule that draft alone is not sufficient; here it is combined with a real unanswered material review.
result.card: This draft PR adds a SIMD-vectorized ChaCha20 implementation aiming for a 2-4x speedup, motivated by profiling showing ChaCha20 consumes roughly 30% of the network thread's CPU during BIP324 encrypted transport handling; l0rinc's independent IBD benchmark showed a real but modest (~3%) end-to-end speedup. The design has been reworked twice in response to deep review (from ajtowns, sipa, l0rinc, maflcko) after a big-endian correctness bug and a GCC-specific performance regression were found and fixed. It remains a draft: commit history is messy, documentation incomplete, and l0rinc's 2026-08-30 review requests smaller commits, more dispatch-path test/fuzz coverage, and reuse of existing helpers, and reports a possible IBD slowdown that has not yet been addressed by the author. Agreement is Disputed rather than clearly positive because that latest substantive review round is unanswered, though the author has consistently engaged with every prior round. No formal dependency, but the author's WIP AVX2/AVX512 follow-up and a planned Poly1305 vectorization both build on this work landing first.
